questions.question: During a trip, carry-on baggage:

options.text: Can be left in the aisle.
Must be stored away from the aisle.
Must be kept on the rider's lap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must be stored away from the aisle.
questions.explanation: Keep the aisles and stairwells clear at all times. Clear aisles prevent passengers from tripping.

questions.question: When a bus stops at an intermediate stop or final destination, passengers should be told:

options.text: The location.
The bus company's name.
The name of the driver.

questions.explanation: The driver should announce where the bus is stopping, why it is stopping, when it will leave, and the bus number.

questions.question: If another driver is tailgating you, you should:

options.text: Move into the left lane.
Speed up.
Increase the distance between you and the vehicle ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase the distance between you and the vehicle ahead.
questions.explanation: When being tailgated, increase your distance from the vehicle ahead. This reduces the need for sudden stops and gives the tailgater room to pass. Do not speed up, as this may make the tailgater continue at a dangerous distance.

questions.question: After a bus trip is completed, the vehicle:

options.text: Should be returned without an inspection.
Should be inspected.
Should be drained of fuel.

questions.explanation: Inspect the bus after every trip. Passengers may have damaged safety items, and these must be repaired before the next trip.

questions.question: When asked to change lanes during the driving test, you should:

options.text: Make the change as soon as asked, without looking.
Use your turn signal and change lanes when safe.
Make the lane change as quickly as possible, even if it means cutting off another driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your turn signal and change lanes when safe.
questions.explanation: During the driving test, you will be asked to change lanes. Check traffic and use proper signals before changing lanes.

questions.question: A driver who stops at a green light could be:

options.text: An impaired driver.
A driver who is color blind.
A person who does not know the rules of the road.

questions.explanation: Watch other drivers for signs of impairment. Drivers who are drunk, tired, on drugs, or sick are dangerous. Stopping at a green light is a sign that a driver may be impaired.

questions.question: A distracted driver:

options.text: Usually follows the rules of the road.
Usually notices hazards more slowly.
Is a good person to follow.

questions.explanation: Distracted drivers see hazards on the road more slowly than focused drivers, or they may not see them at all.

questions.question: Do not base your decision to shift gears on:

options.text: The speed of your engine (rpm).
The speed of the road (mph).
The actions of the vehicle next to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: The actions of the vehicle next to you.
questions.explanation: Shift gears based on your engine's rpm range or your speedometer. Learn which speeds work for each gear. Do not shift based on what other vehicles do.

questions.question: Drivers must have a CDL if operating a vehicle designed to carry at least:

options.text: Three passengers.
15 passengers.
44 passengers.

questions.explanation: You need a commercial driver license to operate a vehicle designed to seat 16 or more people, including the driver.

questions.question: If you must drive in reverse, backing toward the driver's side:

options.text: Is always encouraged.
Is discouraged.
Is only recommended if it is raining.

questions.explanation: Back toward the driver's side when you must reverse. This gives you the best view of your path.

questions.question: If an aggressive driver confronts you, what should you do?

options.text: Make eye contact to communicate with them.
Ignore their gestures.
Do not move out of their way.

questions.explanation: When facing an aggressive driver, get out of their way if you can. Do not make eye contact, as this may make them more angry. Do not respond to their actions or gestures.

questions.question: When you pull over to the side of the road, what should you do?

options.text: Rely on your taillights to warn other drivers.
Do not worry about other drivers.
Turn on your four-way emergency flashers to warn other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your four-way emergency flashers to warn other drivers.
questions.explanation: When stopped on the side of the road, always turn on your four-way emergency flashers. This is especially important when visibility is low. Place warning devices within 10 minutes of stopping.

questions.question: Water pooled on a roadway can cause:

options.text: Hydroplaning.
Acceleration.
Stopping.

questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when water collects on the road surface.

questions.question: If your driving test route does not include a railroad crossing, what happens?

options.text: You will not have to do anything related to crossings.
You may have to explain how to cross railroad tracks.
You will have to take the test again on a route with a railroad crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may have to explain how to cross railroad tracks.
questions.explanation: If your driving test route does not include a railroad crossing, the examiner may ask you to explain and show the correct way to cross railroad tracks at a practice location.

questions.question: How should you do pre-trip inspections?

options.text: Do them differently each time to focus on different items.
Do them the same way each time so you do not forget anything.
Do them once in a while.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do them the same way each time so you do not forget anything.
questions.explanation: Do a pre-trip inspection the same way before every drive. This helps you remember all the steps and makes sure you check everything.

questions.question: Which is NOT a good rule for using turn signals?

options.text: Signal early, before you turn or change lanes.
Signal the entire time you are turning or changing lanes.
Do not over-signal. If no one is near you, do not signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not over-signal. If no one is near you, do not signal.
questions.explanation: Always signal before turning or changing lanes, even if no one is nearby. Signal the whole time you are making your move. Turn off the signal after you finish.

questions.question: When starting from a complete stop, a vehicle should:

options.text: Jerk forward quickly.
Roll backwards.
Not roll backwards.

questions.explanation: Make sure your vehicle does not roll backwards when you start moving from a stop. This helps you avoid hitting vehicles behind you.

questions.question: Black ice is:

options.text: A thick layer of ice on the road.
A thin, clear layer of ice on the road.
Ice that looks black because of road debris.

questions.correctAnswerText: A thin, clear layer of ice on the road.
questions.explanation: Black ice is a thin, clear layer of ice you can see through. The road will look wet. Watch for black ice when the road looks wet and the temperature is below freezing.

questions.question: Too much air pressure in a tire:

options.text: Is not possible.
Is good on long drives.
Can be dangerous.

questions.explanation: Never put too much air pressure in your tires. Check your tire air pressure with a gauge during inspections.

questions.question: How many hours of sleep does an adult need each day to stay alert?

options.text: Six to seven hours
Seven to eight hours
Eight to nine hours
Four to five hours

questions.explanation: Getting enough sleep is important for safe driving. Most adults need eight to nine hours of sleep each night to stay alert.
